explanation: Copperleaf's current ratio of 1.5 is close to the industry's 1.4. Short-term assets cover short-term obligations comfortably without too much money sitting idle.
Higher is not always better. A current ratio of 5 against 1.5 means cash, receivables or stock are piling up unused: idle funds that earn nothing.
Lower is not always better. With almost no debt, Copperleaf is not using borrowings, which are usually cheaper than equity because interest is tax-deductible. Shareholders' returns could be higher.
Higher is not always better. Turning stock 40 times against 8 suggests Copperleaf holds very little stock, so cafés risk running out of beans and losing sales.
Customers take 75 days to pay against an industry norm of 30. Cash is stuck with customers, and some dues may turn bad.
EBIT covers interest only 1.2 times against 6 for the industry. A small fall in profit could leave Copperleaf unable to pay interest.
